March — Painting

Pattern
Painting

Reflection

For this project, I explored layered color to build a dynamic painted surface. The process involved applying loose, textured strokes first, then carving a web-like pattern on top with sharp white lines. Working this way taught me how contrast between structure and spontaneity creates visual energy — rigid lines feel alive precisely because the background is unpredictable. I came away with a much stronger intuition for how line weight and spacing control the sense of depth across a flat canvas.

April — Acrylic

Parody
Painting

Reflection

This project challenged me to take a recognizable character and reinterpret it through a deliberately exaggerated, humorous lens. Using acrylic paint on a large surface, I pushed proportions and expressions toward the absurd. The most valuable lesson was that caricature is a real skill — you have to understand the source deeply before you can convincingly break its rules. Mixing greens consistently across a large area proved far harder to control than I expected.

May — Colored Pencil

Colored
Pencil
Drawing

Reflection

For the final project I worked entirely in colored pencil to create a graffiti-style lettering piece set against a hand-drawn brick wall. Layering colored pencil taught me a great deal about pressure control — building gradients slowly rather than pressing hard early gives far more range to blend with. Designing the letterforms required planning the full composition first so that decorative elements balanced the weight of the letters. This project brought together typography, illustration, and shading into a single satisfying piece.
